positioning: The tailless wonder of the Isle of Man. A round, rabbit-hopping, loyal hunter.
story: The Manx is the cat without a tail, and it comes from the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea. Tailless cats are an ancient island mutation, and the breed is named for the Manx people. Legends say the cat arrived on the Spanish Armada or that it was late to Noah's ark and had its tail caught in the closing door.

The tail is the great variable. The gene is dominant, and in a litter the kittens vary. A rumpy has no tail at all and a small dimple where the tail would be, a rumpy riser has a bump of bone, a stumpy has a short stub, and a longy has a nearly full tail. Only rumpies and risers are normally shown.

The shape is round. A Manx has a round head, round cheeks, a sturdy round body and hind legs that are longer than the front, so that its rump is higher than its shoulders. This gives it a rabbit-like gait, a hop at a gallop, and a strong leap.

The personality is that of a loyal dog. Manx cats are often described as devoted, intelligent and playful, and they can learn to fetch, follow, and wait at the door for their people. They are excellent hunters and have long been prized on farms and ships for catching mice and rats.

The coat comes in short and long versions, and the long version is sometimes called a Cymric. Both have a thick double coat that is easy to care for with a weekly brush. They get on with other pets and are known for a soft voice, a trill and a chirp.

The gene that removes the tail can affect the spine. Manx syndrome, a set of spinal and bowel problems, can appear in some kittens, so choose a breeder who health-tests and breeds responsibly. Keep the cat lean, give it a stable home and expect a loyal companion for a dozen years.
fblocks: From the Isle of Man, where the tailless cats have lived for centuries.
Rumpy, riser, stumpy or longy. The gene is dominant and the litter varies.
A loyal, doglike companion and an excellent mouser.
A thick double coat in almost any color, short for the Manx and long for the Cymric.
An ancient island breed, among the first registered in the cat fancy.
Give it a stable home, a perch and a purpose. It will follow you everywhere.

days: The Manx comes from the Isle of Man, and many have no tail at all.
Legend says the Manx was too late for the ark and lost its tail in the door.
The rump sits higher than the shoulders, and the cat hops like a rabbit.
It brings the toy back, waits at the door and then goes to hunt.
You do not need a tail to find your balance.
Ask who has seen a cat with a bunny hop and no tail to wag.
A round, warm body pressed against your side for the night.
last_walk:
Evening sun on the barn roof, and the grass is high.
The Manx has hunted, hopped and kept watch over the farm all week. Now it sits on the stone wall, round shape against the sky, and listens to the crickets. One more look at the field, then the porch.
cap: The tailless cat of the Isle of Man
